image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on blue water. The duck features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a greyish-brown body, and a yellow-green bill with a black tip. The body is partially submerged, showing a natural floating posture with ripples in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with the characteristic yellow-green coloration and black nail typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is compact and sits low in the water, indicating buoyancy. The plumage texture appears dense and smooth, consistent with waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged beneath the water line and are not visible in this specific pose.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body, appearing broad and tapering towards the tail, consistent with the 'broad and pointed' description when folded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly visible at the rear of the duck.
